kicker: LEDGER · Thursday 22 October · the street, the shop family's sample
title: Rita's front in the street
how: Shortfalls first. At night her window's light is far too strong for the goods: from the hook camera her glass burns white in three patches and the shelves' front edges glow like red and blue neon strips; close up the whites burn and the red velvet stains the pale goods red (set aside after two tries; next, the strip lights under the shelves the cloud designed, at a measured strength), so no night picture is shown. Close up her shiny goods show blocky marks from the cloud's low-quality texture files (set aside too). By day, from the hook camera, the display hardly reads under the street's reflection, RITA'S reads only faintly, PAWNBROKER and the words on the glass not at all, and her fascia is a lighter pink than the fish shop's maroon. The front has no real wear yet (only pale chips on the fascia); the balls read matte, not gilt; the night grille's empty track and the sill's rail are hard dark bars; the goods stand in tidy rows, their price tickets blank, and the clocks have no glass; in her glass the street's reflection shows visible stair-steps along its edges (and along the grey ledge in the small panes above) and the phone kiosk's yellow sign reflects back to front across the left pane, and faintly the right; the sill's marble shows long grey streaks. The lamp columns: a shade darker as you asked, but the grime at the foot is faint, the number plate blank, and the rain staining read as grain after two tries, so they are not done.

The cloud's whole front for Rita's pawnbroker now stands in the street behind the street's own glass (the broken-window crime still works on it): the fascia with RITA'S, the three gilt balls on their bracket, the doors, the 3D display on velvet tiers and her room behind. The hook camera by day, the pavement by day, the front from across the road and the reverse view passed fresh reviewers. Taken today in the game at 2560 by 1440, shown at full size, with the street's people hidden (their clothes are a known open fault); the phone kiosk and the neighbours are the street as it was, and the stack of crates by her window is an old stand-in that reads as one striped block.
foot: Nothing bought or signed up for. Anything you do not pick carries onto the next page.
